reference.title: Smith Low Bar Squat
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Big breath in and brace at the top, hold it on the way down and through the bottom, breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise or at the top.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.load: User-chosen; leave about 2 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5-5 kg when every rep reaches parallel with good form.

cues.text: Bar low on the back, across the rear shoulders just below the bony ridge of the shoulder blades; hands close enough to pin it there, elbows lifted back. Feet about shoulder width, toes turned out; turn the bar off the pegs.
Big breath, brace, then send the hips back and down as the chest tips forward; knees push out over the toes while the bar rides down the rails.
Hips at or just below knee level, back flat, heels down; no bounce.
Drive the hips up and back into the bar while the chest rises with them; knees keep pushing out. Breathe out past the hardest part.
Lock out the hips and knees, take a new breath and brace. After the last rep turn the bar back onto the pegs.

mistakes.fix: Set it just below the ridge of the shoulder blades, squeeze the upper back and grip narrow enough to trap it.

mistakes.mistake: Hips rising faster than the chest (the squat turns into a good morning)
mistakes.fix: Drive the upper back into the bar so hips and shoulders rise together.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bent back carrying the bar
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrists straight and the bar on the back, not in the hands; widen the grip a little if needed.
Push the knees out over the toes.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the lower back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Brace harder and stop just above the depth where the pelvis tucks under.

kinematics.norm: About shoulder width with the toes out (Lorenzetti 2018; Sinclair 2022)
To about thighs parallel (hip crease at the top of the knee), typical of powerlifting depth (Swinton 2012)
More hip flexion and hip extensor demand than a high-bar squat (Swinton 2012; Larsen 2021)
Leans further forward than a high-bar squat, as the low bar must stay over mid-foot (Larsen 2021)
Low bar across the posterior deltoids, a few cm below the high-bar position (Larsen 2021); the bar path is fixed by the rails
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

cautions: Set the safety stops just under the lowest bar position before the first rep; the bar cannot go lower than them.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs (a small turn of the wrists) with an empty bar first.
The rails fix the bar path: place yourself so the movement feels natural for the joints, and do not force range.
The low bar position needs good shoulder mobility; do not force the hands in if the elbows or shoulders hurt.
Keep the back flat: the forward lean puts more load on the lower back.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder or elbow discomfort: widen the grip or use the high-bar position.
Limited hip mobility: squat to a box at parallel.
regressions: Box squat to a parallel box.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: The forward lean and hips-back position give the hip extensors a larger share than in a high-bar squat (Swinton 2012).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: The forward lean and hips-back position give the hip extensors a larger share than in a high-bar squat (Swinton 2012).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Still extend the knees from parallel, with somewhat less knee demand than a high-bar squat (Swinton 2012; Larsen 2021).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Still extend the knees from parallel, with somewhat less knee demand than a high-bar squat (Swinton 2012; Larsen 2021).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus extends the hip from flexion; the shoulder-width stance keeps it busy.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus extends the hip from flexion; the shoulder-width stance keeps it busy.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension against the forward lean.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension against the forward lean.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Work hard to hold the back flat under the forward-leaning trunk.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Work hard to hold the back flat under the forward-leaning trunk.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the lower legs over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the lower legs over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees tracking out over the toes.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees tracking out over the toes.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: The rear delts form the shelf the low bar sits on.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: The rear delts form the shelf the low bar sits on.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Help hold the shoulder blades back under the bar.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Help hold the shoulder blades back under the bar.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.

phases.label: Stand tall, bar low on the back
